experiments.title: A craftsperson withdraws consent to be listed publicly
experiments.plain: Member M0001 still has a listing in the public edition, but their public_opt_in is changed to 0.
experiments.predict: Which rule should catch this, and why is it blocking rather than a warning?
experiments.look_for: contradictory_audience blocks the release and names M0001. The editor's fix then withdraws every public listing for people who did not opt in - now two instead of one - and the release goes ahead without them. Publishing someone who said no is never acceptable, so it cannot be a warning.

safeguards.title: Remove the editor's sign-off
safeguards.predict: The checks pass in scene 3. Without a sign-off step, what happens next - and who is recorded as the approver?
safeguards.look_for: Scene 3 publishes all twelve directories at once - PUBLISHED - and the release record names the approver as "nobody". In the normal run it stops at the freeze step until the directory editor signs off in scene 4.
safeguards.protects: A person must approve the checked data before twelve directories are printed and published.
safeguards.defend: Checks prove the data is valid, not that it is right to publish. A named sign-off puts a person's judgement and name on every release, and the release record shows who it was.
